valkey.title: Valkey Setup Required
valkey.intro: LiteLLM searches documents you have already stored in Valkey. It does not create the index or upload documents for you. Before creating this vector store, make sure:

steps.searchEnabled: Your Valkey server has vector search enabled (the valkey-search module, included in the valkey-bundle image and in AWS ElastiCache / MemoryDB for Valkey)
steps.indexLoaded: You have already created a search index and loaded your documents and their embeddings into it. Enter that index name as the Vector Store ID
steps.embeddingModel: You know which embedding model created those stored embeddings. That model must be added to this proxy under Models so you can pick it below. Using a different model returns wrong results
steps.fieldNames: You know the field names your documents use for their text and their embedding. If they are not "text" and "embedding", set them below

valkey.howItWorks: When a query comes in, LiteLLM converts it to an embedding with the model below and returns the closest matching documents from your index.

opensearch.title: OpenSearch Setup Required
opensearch.intro: LiteLLM searches a k-NN index you already have in an OpenSearch Serverless collection or an OpenSearch Service domain. It does not create the index or upload documents. Before creating this vector store, make sure:

steps.knnField: The index has a knn_vector field holding each document's embedding. Enter the index name as the Vector Store ID, or under Index Name when another endpoint already uses that ID
steps.embeddingModel: You know which embedding model created those embeddings. That model must be added to this proxy under Models so you can pick it below. Using a different model returns wrong results
steps.credentials: The proxy has AWS credentials that can read the index, either its own (environment variables or an IAM role) or a saved credential picked under Existing Credentials. A Serverless collection needs a data access policy for them, and a domain needs its access policy to allow them

vertexAiSearch.title: Vertex AI Search Setup
vertexAiSearch.intro: To use Vertex AI Search (Discovery Engine):
vertexAiSearch.renameNote: Note: Google Cloud has renamed this to "Agent Search" in its console — the steps below still apply.

steps.guide: Enable the Discovery Engine API on your Google Cloud project and create a data store following the guide: <guide>Create a Vertex AI Search data store</guide>
steps.location: Pick a supported location: global, us, or eu
steps.dataStoreId: For most data store types (Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Media): copy the data store ID and enter it in the Vector Store ID field below.
steps.engineId: For website, healthcare, and connector-based sources (Drive, Gmail, Slack, Jira, etc.): create a search app on top of the data store, then copy the Engine ID and enter it in the Engine ID field. The Vector Store ID is still required as the LiteLLM-side name for this record, but it isn't used in the GCP URL when Engine ID is set.

intro.description: Controls the mcp_tool_search virtual tool that native MCP clients call to discover tools. With an embedding model set, tools are ranked by the meaning of their name and description, so a query like "FX" finds a "foreign exchange rates" tool. Without one, keyword matching is used. Callers only ever see tools their key, team and server permissions already allow.

embeddingModel.label: Embedding Model
embeddingModel.hint: Embedding model from your model list used to rank tools by meaning. Clear it to fall back to keyword matching.

topK.label: Top K Results
topK.hint: Most ranked tools a search returns. A smaller top_k in the tool call wins. Core tools do not count.

similarityThreshold.label: Similarity Threshold
similarityThreshold.hint: Lowest cosine similarity a tool needs to appear in semantic results. 0 means no cutoff.

coreTools.label: Always Returned First
coreTools.hint: One tool name per line, e.g. my_server-get_rates. Listed before ranked results whenever the caller is allowed to use them.
